title: Do you think the AI companies have been incorporating binary data in their training data?
author: Dredgefort
selftext:
AI is good at decompiling binaries; we've seen this. But this raises an ethical concern. In their quest for training data, have they been feeding it binaries from all kinds of sources, including games? The training of it would actually be quite simple

Feed AI binary data -> have it decompile it -> recompile the decompiled code back into binary data -> train on the result. 

  
Like if that's the case, it's possible that the training data has actually incorporated the data of real games directly. 

  
I personally think AI companies should be required, by law, to reveal their training sets. I mean they may not have been, but we have no way to know.

replies.author: thumbox1
replies.body:
Because LLMs learn via token sequence and attribute statistical valeu for these tokens, applying and calculating these in binary data requires you to have several low level correctes since the sequence will be always 0 and 1. Also tokenisation is a text process. This is why it works good at code level. Applying similar rules to binary would produce a sequence that cannot easily ensure the prompt is fulfilled. 

Also you need to understand the compilation process will optimise your code depending on the platform, it means that the binary outputs are different. 

Have a look at byte native models. They were design to tread bytes only. They don't solve gaming problem and it can take 4 times more length to have a relevant sequenced token

replies.author: ShenGahMing
replies.body:
>in binary data requires you to have several low level correctes since the sequence will be always 0 and 1

Binary does NOT litterally means 0 or 1.

In this context it means executable files written in machine language.

If a human wants to read/write binary, he would typically do it in hexadecimal. (0-9A-F, 16 symbols).

replies.author: thumbox1
replies.body:
you perfectly understood I meant tokenisation in the current LLM foundation models. If you convert to hexadecimal it's no longer a binary model. Computer science class 101.

Anyways your comment does change anything.

replies.author: ShenGahMing
replies.body:
> Computer science class 101.

Apparently you missed that ALL data is technically binary in memory, and EVERYTHING YOU SEE ON SCREEN is a transformation of binary data.

Tokens too. Vectors embedding too. LLMs too. If you can download it, its binary, ok ?

Since everything is binary, we never say it, which free the word "binary" to encode a different meaning : in this context, a binary file is an executable file in machine code.

That's how language works. Not everything is litteral.
